timeline.draft_answer: Professor Renate Schubert pointed out that air travel in Switzerland is heavily under-taxed compared with other transport. International flights are exempt from fuel tax (unlike petrol for cars), exempt from CO2 tax, have no emissions limits, and air passengers don't pay VAT. As a result, air fares are very low compared with other means of transport — e.g., a flight from Basel to Berlin costs only 31.20 francs, while a regular second-class train ticket costs 178 francs. She raised the question of whether surcharges on flying would make train travel more economically competitive, framing the current situation as flying being 'at the climate's expense.'
